Module com.ecotwin
Package com.ecotwin.service

Class HouseholdService

java.lang.Object
com.ecotwin.service.HouseholdService
public class HouseholdService extends Object
Households and their members: creating and joining (US-08, US-09), leaving and viewing members (US-10, US-11), activity history (US-12, US-13) and administration (US-32 to US-36).

Each household has exactly one administrator. Membership changes are written to the household's activity history. Admin-only actions throw IllegalArgumentException when an ordinary member tries them, and the UI shows that message.

  • Method Details

    • createHousehold

      public Household createHousehold(User creator, String name, int occupants, String dwellingType, String state)
      US-08: creator becomes admin, household persists after restart.
      Parameters:
      creator - the signed-in user creating the household; they become its admin
      name - the household's name
      occupants - how many people live there (at least 1); scores are per person
      dwellingType - e.g. "House" or "Apartment"
      state - the Australian state, e.g. "QLD"
      Returns:
      the new household, with a unique 6-character join code
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the name is blank or occupants is less than 1

    • joinHousehold

      public Household joinHousehold(User user, String joinCode)
      US-09: join by code; invalid code raises an error the UI turns into "No household found with that code". The code is trimmed and upper-cased first, so " 95fcve" works.
      Parameters:
      user - the signed-in user joining
      joinCode - the code shared by the household's admin
      Returns:
      the household joined, with the user added as an ordinary member
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the code is blank or matches no household

    • generateUniqueJoinCode

      private String generateUniqueJoinCode()
      Makes a random 6-character code, retrying until no other household uses it. Letters and digits that look alike (0/O, 1/I) are left out so codes are easy to read out.
      Returns:
      a join code no household currently has
